questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits.)

(2, 125, 3)

(1, 64, 3)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

**Logic: (First number + Third number)³** **= Second number.**

1) (2, 125, 3)

⇒ (2 + 3)³ ⇒ (5)³ = 125

And,

2) (1, 64, 3)

⇒ (1 + 3)3 ⇒ (4)3 = 64

Let's check each option one by one:

**Option 1) **(2, 100, 8)

⇒ (2 + 8) 3 ⇒ (10)3 = 1000 ≠ 100 (Incorrect)

**Option 2) **(5, 512, 3)

⇒ (5 + 3)3 ⇒ (8)3 = 512 (Correct)

**Option 3) **(12, 50, 13)

⇒ (12 + 13)3 ⇒ (25)3 = 15625 ≠ 50 (Incorrect)

**Option 4) **(4, 341, 3)

⇒ (4 + 3)3 ⇒ (7)3 = 343 ≠ 341 (Incorrect)

Hence, the correct answer is **"(5, 512, 3)"**

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term.

10 : 45 :: ? : 28 :: 11 : 55
questions.solution:
**Logic: (First number ÷ 2) × (First number - 1) = Second number**

10 : 45 →

⇒ (10/2) × (10 -1) = 5 × 9 = 45

And, 

11 : 55 →

⇒ (11/2) × (11 -1) = (11/2) × 10 = 11 × 5 = 55

Similarly,

**? : 28 →**

⇒ (x/2) × (x -1) = 28

⇒ x(x - 1) = 56

⇒ x² - x - 56 = 0 

⇒ (x - 8)(x + 7) = 0

**⇒ x = either 8 or -7**

**As value can not be negative here. So, the correct value will be 8.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"8".**

questions.question:
By interchanging the given two signs which of the following equation will be correct?

+ and ÷
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Interchanging the given two signs so that the given equation will be correct.

**Given: **+ and ÷ 

Let's check each option one by one:

**Option 1) **9 × 18 + 27 ÷ 36 – 30 = 18

After interchanging the mathematical signs we get the:

⇒ 9 × __**18 ÷ 27**__ + 36 – 30 = 18

⇒ __**9 × 0.666**__ + 36 - 30 = 18

⇒ __**5.994 + 36**__ - 30 = 18

⇒ __**41.994 - 30**__ = 18

⇒ 11.994 ≠ 18

⇒ **LHS ≠ RHS**

**Option 2) **9 + 3 × 2 – 8 ÷ 1 = –1

After interchanging the mathematical signs we get the:

⇒ __**9 ÷ 3**__ × 2 – 8 + 1 = –1

⇒ __**3 × 2**__ - 8 + 1 = - 1

⇒ __**6**__ - 8 + __**1**__ = - 1

⇒ __**7 - 8**__ = -1

⇒ - 1 = - 1

⇒ **LHS = RHS**

**Option 3) **16 + 8 × 2 ÷ 6 – 9 = 10

After interchanging the mathematical signs we get the:

⇒ __**16 ÷ 8**__ × 2 + 6 – 9 = 10

⇒ __**2 × 2 **__+ 6 - 9 = 10

⇒ __**4 + 6**__ - 9 = 10

⇒ 10 - 9 = 10

⇒ 1 ≠ 10 

⇒ **LHS ≠ RHS**

**Option 4) **16 + 2 × 6 ÷ 3 – 7 = 50

After interchanging the mathematical signs we get the:

⇒ __**16 ÷ 2**__ × 6 + 3 – 7 = 50

⇒ 8 × 6 + 3 - 7 = 50

⇒ 48 +3 - 7 = 50

⇒ 51 - 7 = 50

⇒ 44 ≠ 50

⇒ **LHS ≠ RHS**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow (s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some mice are keyboards.

All keyboards are CPUs.

All mice are webcams.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some CPUs are mice.

II. Some webcams are keyboards.

III. Some webcams are CPUs.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

The least possible Venn diagram is shown below according to the given information.

Statements:

Some mice are keyboards.

All keyboards are CPUs.

All mice are webcams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aad8dd3aebb00d493fd38a93bc71b36a5407f4a4623779f3239f99bb42b989b9.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some CPUs are mice → **Follow **→ As some mice are keyboards and all keyboards are CPUs. So some CPUs are mice is definitely followed.

II. Some webcams are keyboards → Follow → As Some mice are keyboards and all mice are webcams. So some webcams are keyboards definitely followed.

III. Some webcams are CPUs → Follow → As Some mice are keyboards, all keyboards are CPUs and All mice are webcams. So some webcams are CPUs is definitely followed.

So, All conclusions are follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

questions.question:
After interchanging the given two numbers and two signs what will be the values of equations ( I ) and ( II ) respectively?

× and –, 4 and 5

I. 9 ÷ 3 × 6 + 5 – 4

II. 5 – 4 × 3 + 6 ÷ 2
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Here in this question interchanging the given two numbers and two signs in the given equation.

**Given: **× and –, 4 and 5

I. 9 ÷ 3 × 6 + 5 – 4

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs we get the;

⇒ __**9 ÷ 3**__ - 6 + 4 × 5

⇒ 3 - 6 + __**4 × 5**__

⇒ __**3**__ - 6 __**+ 20**__

⇒ __**23 - 6**__

⇒ 17

II. 5 – 4 × 3 + 6 ÷ 2 

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs we get the;

⇒ 4 × 5 - 3 + __**6 ÷ 2 **__

⇒ __**4 × 5**__ - 3 + 3

⇒ __**20**__ - 3 __**+ 3**__

⇒ __**23 - 3**__

⇒ 20

Hence, the correct answer is **"17 , 20".**
